title: TS SDK: stream-gate duplex shim for resilient AsyncIterator <-> WebStream handoff
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a tiny, focused abstraction (stream-gate + duplex-shim) in the TypeScript SDK that normalizes backpressure, cancellation, and error propagation between AsyncIterator-based consumers and Web Streams producers. Current customer patterns mix AsyncIterator and ReadableStream, leading to subtle cancellation leaks, unbounded buffering, and ergonomics friction (multiple utility shims across apps). This ticket defines the API, implements the runtime shim, and ships examples and tests. Goal: a single recommended interoperable surface that preserves the strongest semantics of both sides and is easy to adopt in app code and examples.
acceptance_criteria: Exports createStreamGate(input: AsyncIterable | ReadableStream) and createDuplexShim({ readable, writable }): Duplex that maps AsyncIterator <-> WebStream with correct backpressure semantics
Cancellation initiated by consumer (for-await) must cancel upstream request/HTTP stream and release underlying resources
Backpressure signaled from writable (consumer) must pause upstream reads (no unbounded buffering) and resume when ready
Errors on either side surface as single normalized error observable on both consumers
Comprehensive unit and integration tests exercising Node/Deno/browser combos
Docs + 3 usage examples (chat streaming, embedding chunked upload, long-polling fallback) merged
Compatibility tests in CI across Node 18/20 and Chromium/ws environments
implementation_notes: Design a small runtime primitive: StreamGate which keeps a bounded in-memory slot (configurable) and translates pull signals into upstream reads
Expose two convenience helpers: readableFromAsyncIterator(iterator, opts) and asyncIteratorFromReadable(stream, opts)
Implement duplexShim to create a pair { readable: ReadableStream, writable: WritableStream } where writable writes as AsyncIterator consumer and readable yields data from producer
Propagate cancellation by wiring AbortSignal: consumer cancellation aborts the gate's signal which triggers upstream close and emits a standardized CancelError
Default slot size 1 to minimize latency while still allowing short buffering for transformer steps; make it tunable via options
Keep runtime code dependency-free and small (no third-party libs). Use platform feature-detection for ReadableStream/TransformStream availability and fall back to polyfills in tests only
Expose TypeScript overloads for both browser and node-friendly types (AsyncIterable<Uint8Array | string>), and provide JSDoc examples
design_decisions: Favor single-slot by default to preserve low tail latency while preventing immediate backpressure thrashing
Represent cancellation as a single normalized CancelError type in the SDK so callers can compare instanceof CancelError rather than string matching
Avoid automatic data coalescing; SDK provides small utility compose helpers separately if callers want coalescing or framing
Do not attempt to fully emulate all ReadableStream backpressure semantics; map readable.desiredSize >= 1 -> resume, <= 0 -> pause. Keep mapping deterministic across platforms
test_plan: Unit tests: stream-gate basic push/pull, cancellation, error propagation (Node environment)
Integration: spawn a tiny local HTTP server that returns chunked responses; exercise AsyncIterator reader -> duplexShim -> writable consumer; assert no unbounded memory growth
Cross-runtime tests: run browser headless test (Playwright) for Web Stream paths and Deno for native AsyncIterator semantics
Fuzz test: randomized delays on producer/consumer and ensure no deadlocks for 60s runs
Performance microbench: measure end-to-end latency and throughput for slot sizes [1,4,16] and include in PR benchmark artifact
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag `ts_stream_gate` in SDK v2 beta. Release beta with docs site example. Enable flag for early adopter customers via console toggles. Collect telemetry (errors, cancellation rate, slot-size overrides) for 2 weeks before enabling by default in runtime-1.22 release.
risks: Edge-case differences between Node's stream semantics and browser ReadableStream could expose race conditions
Misconfiguration of slot size by users could cause increased latency or head-of-line blocking
If cancellation semantics leak, long-lived generator functions may keep resources alive (memory / file handles)
Polyfill complexity for older runtimes might bloat the SDK if not carefully gated
notes: We intentionally avoid naming this 'bridge' to reduce users reaching for broad semantics; 'stream-gate' signals the flow-control focus
Early feedback from Solutions Eng (Anna R.) suggested default slot=1 to minimize chat latency — we adopted that
Related internal tickets: ENG-27781 (cancellation propagation research) - add as dependency
related_links: https://playwright.dev/ - used for browser test harness
